items.title: Pakistan Opens Crypto Licensing Portal With Deadline
points: Pakistan launched an official crypto licensing portal, establishing a regulated framework for exchanges and digital asset service providers.
The move follows years of regulatory uncertainty in Pakistan's crypto market, now replaced with formal compliance requirements.
Applicants face a firm deadline to submit applications; missing it means being unable to operate as a compliant entity in the country.
The step positions Pakistan alongside other nations adopting standardized crypto oversight rather than outright bans or full deregulation.

items.title: Crypto Rally: Bitcoin and XRP Surge Ahead of Jackson Hole
points: Bitcoin surged above $77,000 on a 21% weekly gain while XRP jumped 46%, driven by US Treasury liquidity moves and an SEC crypto regulatory proposal.

The rally diverged from declines in Asian equities (Samsung, Alibaba) and comes ahead of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, a key watch point for rate signals that could reshape risk-asset positioning.
Institutional positioning is shifting: Paul Tudor Jones raised his IBIT (a Bitcoin ETF, or exchange-traded fund that tracks Bitcoin's price) stake 18.9% to 688,529 shares ($22.9M) as of June 30.
Citigroup announced Bitcoin custody services before year-end, and VanEck leadership told staff to accumulate rather than wait for lower prices.
Ethereum is outperforming Bitcoin in this rally, suggesting early-stage rotation into altcoins (cryptocurrencies other than Bitcoin) beyond Bitcoin maximalism.

items.title: Circle's Arc L2 Launch: Institutional Blockchain Goes Public
points: Circle's Arc blockchain launches September 16 as a permissioned proof-of-authority chain (a blockchain design where only pre-approved entities validate transactions, unlike fully open networks), with founding validators including Circle, BlackRock, DTCC, Mastercard, Standard Chartered, and Visa (~20 validators at launch).
The public testnet processed 671.5 million transactions across 2.8 million wallets; over 100 partners are active on private mainnet, with Uniswap committing to day-one deployment on public mainnet.

Arc is EVM-compatible (Ethereum Virtual Machine compatible, meaning existing Ethereum apps can run on it without code changes) and settles transaction fees in USDC, tying it into Circle's stablecoin infrastructure.
The chain stays permissioned at the validator level even as it opens to public users, balancing institutional control with public participation.

items.title: Bitcoin Maximalism's Ideological Death
points: Bitcoin maximalism (the belief that Bitcoin should be the sole dominant cryptocurrency and function as a global payment currency) is now ideologically dead as its core predictions failed to materialize.
The movement sustains failed predictions through unfalsifiable excuses ('not yet,' 'too early') rather than updating beliefs, paralleling 19th-century Millerism's failed apocalypse predictions.
Bitcoin's actual success came as a regulated, institutionally-custodied store-of-value asset—the opposite of the sovereign payment system maximalists predicted.
The Lightning Network (Bitcoin's layer-2 scaling solution intended to enable everyday payments) failed to achieve mass adoption, undermining the 'Bitcoin as money' thesis.

items.title: Stablecoins' Real Edge vs. Cross-Border Payment Hype
points: Fintechs like Wise already solved cross-currency transfers via pre-funded local currency pools and flow netting, cutting correspondent banking costs from ~15% to under 1% with near-instant settlement—stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to a stable asset like the US dollar) don't improve on this.
Stablecoins' real advantage is narrower: dollar-to-dollar transfers, reaching unbanked recipients without fintech access, 24/7 settlement, and crypto-native workflow integration.
The 'stablecoins will revolutionize remittances' narrative conflates the legacy SWIFT banking problem with today's already-disrupted fintech market.

USDC's stablecoin supply grew $1.7B in one week, and Bernstein raised Circle's price target to $140 (59% upside), citing broader tokenization and stablecoin payment trends rather than cross-border disruption.

items.title: Circle's Valuation Consensus Problem
points: Circle's revenue model (yield on turnover plus stablecoin circulation velocity) doesn't fit the standard interbank-fee framework analysts use for payment companies.
This mismatch leaves Wall Street without a clear valuation methodology, rather than the company being simply mispriced.
Bernstein's $140 price target (59% upside from $87.98) reflects strong conviction, but broader analyst divergence shows no consensus pricing framework exists yet for stablecoin-native businesses.

items.title: Tokenized Equities Volume Explodes
points: Tokenized equity spot trading (buying/selling blockchain-based digital tokens that represent shares of stock) jumped 50x year-over-year to $6B in monthly volume.
This still represents only 0.04% of total US equity trading volume, implying large potential upside if adoption reaches the projected $8.3 trillion market by 2030.
